minutes.headline: Select Board adopted the Finance Committee's written financial policies and appointed four to the Council on Aging.
minutes.summary: The board ratified two reserve police officers, approved a Boys and Girls Club voluntary toll, and interviewed a Council on Aging candidate. It heard the Finance Committee chair present new written financial policies, which were accepted with no opposition. It also discussed expanding MART bus service, electricity aggregation rates and the old school property question.

public_comment.topic: Police chief reported on Lake Shirley patrols and introduced a new police dog (official, not public comment).
Boys and Girls Club representative requested a voluntary toll on October 4.

budget_items.what_was_said: Policy sets a minimum for stabilization funds as a share of the omnibus budget, with the general fund at a lower minimum.
The finance committee reserve stays at its current level.
Free cash priorities: replenish stabilization, then roads and signage, then one-time items; a transfer into stabilization was noted for FY15.
Defines a capital item and debt exclusion process; a board member questioned whether the threshold is too low.
Debt service on non-excluded debt should stay under a share of the budget or levy.
The town pays into the transportation assessment, and a share could be redirected to MART to fund extended bus trips.
Two warrants were read, the second tied to the school building project.

what_happened.line: The Select Board adopted the financial policies recommended by the Finance Committee, with no opposition recorded.
The board appointed four named members to the Council on Aging.
The board ratified two reserve police officer appointments and approved a voluntary toll for the Boys and Girls Club.
On MART bus service, the board took no vote of support and will refine its quote request, include disabled riders, and consider a public hearing.
The town manager is to invite electric aggregation consultants to next week's meeting, as the current rate is expected to rise.

why_it_matters: The adopted policies set the town's rules for reserves, free cash use, capital items and borrowing limits, which shape how future budgets and debt exclusion requests reach voters.
Redirecting part of the town's transportation assessment to MART, and the electric aggregation rate, could change what residents pay or the services they get, but neither has been decided.
watch_next: Next week's meeting: electric aggregation consultants are to be invited, and the town manager is to bring back public access appointments.
A refined MART quote request and a possible public hearing on bus needs.
